extracted.intended_audience: agency officials, regulatory attorneys, administrative-law practitioners, and members of the public seeking definitions and procedural requirements under the Administrative Procedure Act and recent statutory amendments
extracted.subtask_description: Section 551 of Title 5 defines key terms used throughout the Administrative Procedure Act and the page also reproduces related statutory requirements (notably the Administrative Pay‑As‑You‑Go provisions) that impose procedural duties on agencies regarding covered administrative actions that affect direct spending.

rubrics_metrics.name: agency
rubrics_metrics.description: “agency” means each authority of the Government of the United States, whether or not it is within or subject to review by another agency, but does not include—(A) the Congress; (B) the courts of the United States; (C) the governments of the territories or possessions of the United States; (D) the government of the District of Columbia; or except as to the requirements of section 552 of this title—(E) agencies composed of representatives of the parties or of representatives of organizations of the parties to the disputes determined by them; (F) courts martial and military commissions; (G) military authority exercised in the field in time of war or in occupied territory; or (H) functions conferred by sections 1738, 1739, 1743, and 1744 of title 12; subchapter II of chapter 471 of title 49; or sections 1884, 1891–1902, and former section 1641(b)(2), of title 50, appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory definition used throughout the subchapter; several categories are explicitly excluded. Historical notes and later statutory changes (amendments) are provided on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: person
rubrics_metrics.description: “person” includes an individual, partnership, corporation, association, or public or private organization other than an agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to distinguish private and public entities for purposes of agency proceedings and other provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: party
rubrics_metrics.description: “party” includes a person or agency named or admitted as a party, or properly seeking and entitled as of right to be admitted as a party in an agency proceeding, and a person or agency admitted by an agency as a party for limited purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers entities formally participating in agency proceedings, including limited-purpose admissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: rule
rubrics_metrics.description: “rule” means the whole or a part of an agency statement of general or particular applicability and future effect designed to implement, interpret, or prescribe law or policy or describing the organization, procedure, or practice requirements of an agency and includes the approval or prescription for the future of rates, wages, corporate or financial structures or reorganizations thereof, prices, facilities, appliances, services or allowances therefor or of valuations, costs, or accounting, or practices bearing on any of the foregoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad statutory definition encompassing regulatory statements and many agency-prescribed standards or valuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: rule making
rubrics_metrics.description: “rule making” means agency process for formulating, amending, or repealing a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the procedural concept of rulemaking used elsewhere in the APA.

rubrics_metrics.name: order
rubrics_metrics.description: “order” means the whole or a part of a final disposition, whether affirmative, negative, injunctive, or declaratory in form, of an agency in a matter other than rule making but including licensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory meaning of final agency adjudicative dispositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: “adjudication” means agency process for the formulation of an order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines agency adjudicative processes as those producing orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: license
rubrics_metrics.description: “license” includes the whole or a part of an agency permit, certificate, approval, registration, charter, membership, statutory exemption or other form of permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers a wide variety of agency-granted permissions treated as licenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: “licensing” includes agency process respecting the grant, renewal, denial, revocation, suspension, annulment, withdrawal, limitation, amendment, modification, or conditioning of a license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers the full lifecycle of agency license decisions and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: “sanction” includes the whole or a part of an agency—(A) prohibition, requirement, limitation, or other condition affecting the freedom of a person; (B) withholding of relief; (C) imposition of penalty or fine; (D) destruction, taking, seizure, or withholding of property; (E) assessment of damages, reimbursement, restitution, compensation, costs, charges, or fees; (F) requirement, revocation, or suspension of a license; or (G) taking other compulsory or restrictive action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates forms of agency coercive actions that qualify as sanctions; useful for determining when an agency action is punitive or restrictive.

rubrics_metrics.name: relief
rubrics_metrics.description: “relief” includes the whole or a part of an agency—(A) grant of money, assistance, license, authority, exemption, exception, privilege, or remedy; (B) recognition of a claim, right, immunity, privilege, exemption, or exception; or (C) taking of other action on the application or petition of, and beneficial to, a person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies positive agency actions or recognitions constituting relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: agency proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: “agency proceeding” means an agency process as defined by paragraphs (5), (7), and (9) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references definitions of rule making (5), adjudication (7), and licensing (9) to define the universe of agency proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: agency action
rubrics_metrics.description: “agency action” includes the whole or a part of an agency rule, order, license, sanction, relief, or the equivalent or denial thereof, or failure to act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very broad formulation used to capture nearly all agency decisions and inactions for statutory purposes (e.g., judicial review provisions elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: ex parte communication
rubrics_metrics.description: “ex parte communication” means an oral or written communication not on the public record with respect to which reasonable prior notice to all parties is not given, but it shall not include requests for status reports on any matter or proceeding covered by this subchapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines prohibited or regulated off‑the‑record communications in agency proceedings, with a specified exception for status report requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAYGO — administrative_action (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: In this title—(1) the term ‘administrative action’ means a ‘rule’ as defined in section 804(3) of title 5, United States Code;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the Administrative Pay‑As‑You‑Go provisions, 'administrative action' is tied to the definition of 'rule' in another statutory section; this frames which agency acts are subject to PAYGO procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAYGO — agency (narrowed definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: In this title—(2) the term ‘agency’ means any authority of the United States that is an ‘agency’ under section 3502(1) of title 44, United States Code, other than those considered to be independent regulatory agencies, as defined in section 3502(5) of such title;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PAYGO provisions use a more specific cross‑reference to define which agencies are covered; independent regulatory agencies are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: covered discretionary administrative action
rubrics_metrics.description: In this title—(3) the term ‘covered discretionary administrative action’ means a discretionary administrative action that would affect direct spending;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers PAYGO procedural requirements for discretionary administrative actions that have budgetary effects on direct spending.

rubrics_metrics.name: direct spending
rubrics_metrics.description: In this title—(4) the term ‘direct spending’ has the meaning given that term in section 250(c) of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985 (2 U.S.C. 900(c));
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct spending is defined by cross‑reference to the Budget Act; practitioners must consult that statutory definition when applying PAYGO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director (OMB Director)
rubrics_metrics.description: In this title—(5) the term ‘Director’ means the Director of the Office of Management and Budget;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the OMB Director as the official with review and waiver authority under the PAYGO provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: discretionary administrative action (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: In this title—(6) the term ‘discretionary administrative action’—(A) means any administrative action that is not required by law; and (B) includes an administrative action required by law for which an agency has discretion in the manner in which to implement the administrative action;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes truly discretionary actions from those required by law but implemented with agency discretion (both potentially included).

rubrics_metrics.name: increase direct spending (definition, scope for offsets)
rubrics_metrics.description: In this title—(7) the term ‘increase direct spending’ means that the amount of direct spending would increase relative to—(A) the most recently submitted projection of the amount of direct spending presented in baseline estimates ...; (B) with respect to a discretionary administrative action that is incorporated into the applicable projection ... a projection of the amount of direct spending if no administrative action were taken; or (C) with respect to a discretionary administrative action described in paragraph (6)(B), a projection of the amount of direct spending under the least costly implementation option reasonably identifiable by the agency that meets the requirements under the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how increases in direct spending are to be measured (baseline comparisons and least‑cost implementation options) for PAYGO purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement — submit written notice to Director before finalizing covered discretionary administrative action
rubrics_metrics.description: Before an agency may finalize any covered discretionary administrative action, the head of the agency shall submit to the Director for review written notice regarding the covered discretionary administrative action, which shall include an estimate of the budgetary effects of the covered discretionary administrative action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory pre‑finalization submission to OMB with budget estimate; applies to covered discretionary actions that affect direct spending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement — offsets and Director review for actions that increase direct spending
rubrics_metrics.description: If the covered discretionary administrative action would increase direct spending, the written notice ... shall include a proposal to undertake 1 or more other administrative actions that would provide a reduction in direct spending greater than or equal to the increase ... The Director shall determine whether the reduction in direct spending in a proposal ... is greater than or equal to the increase ... If the written notice ... does not include a proposal to offset the increased direct spending as determined ... the Director shall return the written notice to the agency for resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must propose offsetting administrative actions for net increases in direct spending; OMB reviews and can return notices lacking adequate offsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement — nondiscretionary actions that increase direct spending (agency obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency determines that an administrative action that would increase direct spending is required by law and therefore is not a covered discretionary administrative action, before the agency finalizes that administrative action, the head of the agency shall—(1) submit to the Director a written opinion by the general counsel of the agency, or the equivalent employee of the agency, explaining that legal conclusion; (2) submit to the Director a projection of the amount of direct spending under the least costly implementation option reasonably identifiable by the agency that meets the requirements under the statute; and (3) consult with the Director regarding implementation of the administrative action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when an action is legally required, agencies must document legal basis, identify least‑cost implementation, and consult with OMB before finalizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projections methodology requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any projection for purposes of this title shall be conducted in accordance with Office of Management and Budget Circular A–11, or any successor thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires use of OMB Circular A‑11 methodology (or successor) for budgetary projections used under these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of administrative guidance (OMB instruction deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Director shall issue instructions regarding the implementation of this title, including how covered discretionary administrative actions that increase direct spending and nontax receipts will be evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB must promptly issue implementing instructions specifying evaluation procedures and how to apply the PAYGO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver authority and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may waive the requirements of section 263 if the Director concludes that the waiver—(1) is necessary for the delivery of essential services; or (2) is necessary for effective program delivery. Any waiver determination under subsection (a) shall be published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB has discretionary waiver authority in narrowly described circumstances; waiver decisions must be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption thresholds (when title does not apply)
rubrics_metrics.description: This title shall not apply to administrative actions with direct spending cost of less than—(1) $1,000,000,000 over the 10‑year period beginning with the current year; or (2) $100,000,000 in any given year during such 10‑year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes monetary thresholds below which administrative actions are exempt from the PAYGO requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No judicial review of PAYGO determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: No determination, finding, action, or omission under this title shall be subject to judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory bar on courts reviewing decisions, findings, or omissions under the PAYGO title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunset of PAYGO title
rubrics_metrics.description: This title shall expire on December 31, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporal limitation on the statutory authority; practitioners should note the expiration date.

rubrics_metrics.name: GAO report requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 180 days of the date of enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General shall issue a report on the implementation of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAO must assess initial implementation and report to Congress within 180 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study on use of administrative subpoenas — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Not later than December 31, 2001, the Attorney General, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, shall complete a study on the use of administrative subpoena power ... Such report shall include—(1) a description of the sources of administrative subpoena power and the scope of such subpoena power within executive branch agencies; (2) a description of applicable subpoena enforcement mechanisms; (3) a description of any notification provisions and any other provisions relating to safeguarding privacy interests; (4) a description of the standards governing the issuance of administrative subpoenas; and (5) recommendations ... regarding necessary steps to ensure that administrative subpoena power is used and enforced consistently and fairly by executive branch agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the topics the Attorney General's study must address, including scope, enforcement, privacy safeguards, issuance standards, and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report on frequency of administrative subpoenas (limited duration)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attorney General and the Secretary of the Treasury shall report in January of each year to the Committees on the Judiciary of the Senate and the House of Representatives on the number of administrative subpoenas issued by them under this section and the identity of the agency or component ... The reporting requirement of this subsection shall terminate in 3 years after the date of the enactment of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires yearly quantitative reporting of subpoenas and issuing components for a three‑year period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation instructions following revocation of prior Executive Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Office of Management and Budget and the heads of agencies shall promptly take steps to rescind any orders, rules, regulations, guidelines, or policies, or portions thereof, implementing or enforcing the Executive Orders identified, and if rescission cannot be finalized immediately, shall promptly take steps to provide all available exemptions authorized by any such orders ... any personnel positions, committees, task forces, or other entities established pursuant to the Executive Orders ... shall be abolished, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs agency heads and OMB to rescind implementing measures of specified Executive Orders, provide temporary exemptions where immediate rescission is infeasible, and abolish positions/structures created by those EOs, subject to the APA and applicable law.
